texts: good. the collecting parses with Pell as the collector, the silken threads as what was collected, the Cliff Path lanterns as the source, and day 1 / Year 1 / dawn all carried as separate time terms.

mixed: the swarm-level facts are all there — the moths landed on the lanterns, at night, and before Pell's collecting — but nothing records that each moth landed, so a moth named later cannot be tied back to this landing. A bare first-mention plural is what loses it; give the swarm an explicit quantity, as the day-3 episode does, and the per-moth reading comes with it: "Many nightmoths had landed on the lanterns during the night."

mixed: the threads (correctly the same ones Pell collected), the lanterns, the moths as the depositors and the ordering before Pell's collecting are all right, and the threads are rightly recorded as unchanged by the leaving — but again only the swarm as a whole is credited, with no per-moth record. Write: "Each of the nightmoths had left silken threads on the lanterns."
good. Pell, the threads and Cauldron Hall as the destination all land, with Cauldron Hall recorded as a named hall.

mixed: the filling, the three cauldrons, the sea-water and its origin all parse cleanly, but the plural name "the Salt-bloom Tide-pools" is recorded as a single tide-pool — the translator has no way to say that a named place is a SET of pools. If the plurality matters, write: "Hesper filled the three cauldrons with sea-water from the tide-pools of Salt-bloom."
good. Hesper as the boiler, the silken threads as the thing changed by the boiling, the sea-water as where it happened, and past tense are all present.
good. the mire-essence gets its own referent (so the later mentions point back at it), the three cauldrons are its place, and "by evening" is carried as a deadline rather than an exact time.

good. the storing parses with Hesper, the mire-essence as what was stored and three clay vessels as the place, with both the count and the material kept, and it makes no claim about where the vessels sit afterwards.
